claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys are intended for high-temperature structural applications.
Controlled boronizing of an RHEA surface will form a high-entropy boride layer.
The boride layer produced by boronizing will be continuous and adherent.
The high-entropy boride layer will be thermodynamically stable at high temperatures.
The boride layer will inhibit oxygen diffusion into the RHEA.
Inhibiting oxygen diffusion will reduce the rate and extent of oxide-scale formation.
Boronized RHEAs will have significantly thinner oxide scales than untreated RHEAs.
Boronized RHEAs will exhibit lower oxidation-related weight gain than untreated RHEAs.
Boronized RHEAs will preserve their mechanical integrity better than untreated RHEAs during high-temperature oxidation.
Untreated RHEAs generally undergo pronounced oxidation and substantial oxide-scale growth under the proposed high-temperature exposure.
The proposed oxidation-resistance improvement should operate at approximately 1300°C in air or pure oxygen for exposures up to 100 hours.
The improvement will be effective only above approximately 1200°C because boron diffusion and boride-formation kinetics are favorable there.
Significant changes in temperature or oxygen partial pressure may alter the treatment's effectiveness.
Oxide-scale thickness can be compared by cross-sectional SEM, surface phases by XRD and EDS, and oxidation by weight-gain measurements.
